note.explanation: A chemical bond is the force of attraction that holds atoms together. Atoms can form bonds by transferring electrons, sharing electrons, or sharing a pair of electrons donated by one atom.
examples: Sodium transfers one electron to chlorine, forming Na⁺ and Cl⁻; their attraction forms an ionic bond.
Two hydrogen atoms share an electron pair to form H—H, a single covalent bond.
note.checkAnswer: A covalent bond is formed by mutual sharing of an electron pair provided by the bonded atoms.
note.simple: Atoms stick together because they attract each other. They may transfer electrons or share them to make a bond.
note.title: How atoms form chemical bonds
steps: Identify whether electrons are transferred or shared.
For an ionic bond, show the electron transfer and the ions formed.
For a covalent bond, show the shared electron pair or bond line.
For a coordinate covalent bond, identify the donor, acceptor and direction of the arrow.
note.answer: Atoms form chemical bonds by transferring or sharing electrons, or by one atom donating a shared pair.

options: A force of attraction between atoms that holds them together
A force that makes electrons leave the nucleus
A group of atoms with no attraction between them
A transfer of protons between atoms
rationales: Correct: a chemical bond is a force of attraction that holds atoms together.
Incorrect: electron loss may occur during some reactions, but it is not the definition of a bond.
Incorrect: a bond holds atoms together rather than describing atoms without attraction.
Incorrect: the section describes electron transfer or sharing, not proton transfer.

options: Atoms share electrons equally
Electrons are completely transferred from one atom to another
One atom donates a shared electron pair to another
The nuclei of two atoms are transferred
mcqs.stem: Which process forms an ionic bond?
rationales: Incorrect: equal sharing describes a non-polar covalent bond.
Correct: an ionic bond forms by complete transference of electron or electrons from one atom to another.
Incorrect: donation of a shared pair by one atom describes a coordinate covalent bond.
Incorrect: nuclei are not transferred to form an ionic bond.

options: The atoms share an electron pair provided by the bonded atoms
One atom transfers a proton to another
The atoms attract because they have opposite ionic charges
One atom donates both electrons in a shared pair
mcqs.stem: How is a single covalent bond formed?
rationales: Correct: a single covalent bond is formed by mutual sharing of an electron pair provided by the bonded atoms.
Incorrect: proton transfer is not how the section defines a covalent bond.
Incorrect: attraction between oppositely charged ions is the basis of an ionic bond.
Incorrect: donation of both shared electrons by one atom describes a coordinate covalent bond.

mcqs.stem: Which structural formula represents a double covalent bond?
rationales: Incorrect: H—H has one line and represents a single covalent bond.
Correct: O=O has two lines and represents a double covalent bond.
Incorrect: N≡N has three lines and represents a triple covalent bond.
Incorrect: Na⁺Cl⁻ represents oppositely charged ions, not a double covalent bond.

options: The shared pair lies midway between the atoms
The shared pair bends towards the more electronegative atom
Electrons are completely transferred to the less electronegative atom
The shared pair is donated by a third atom
mcqs.stem: What happens to the shared electron pair in a polar covalent bond?
rationales: Incorrect: a pair midway between identical atoms gives a non-polar covalent bond.
Correct: in a bond between non-identical atoms, the shared pair bends towards the more electronegative atom.
Incorrect: the section describes a shared pair bending towards the more electronegative atom, not complete transfer to the less electronegative atom.
Incorrect: a coordinate covalent bond involves donation by one of the bonded species, not a third atom.

options: The donor
The acceptor

mcqs.stem: In a coordinate covalent bond, what is the name for the species that donates the electron pair?
rationales: Correct: the species which donates the electron pair is called the donor.
Incorrect: the species that accepts the electron pair is called the acceptor.
Incorrect: number of shells does not define the donor.
Incorrect: proton loss does not define the donor in a coordinate covalent bond.

options: An arrow pointing towards the donor
An arrow pointing towards the acceptor
A pair of parallel lines
A plus sign between the bonded atoms
mcqs.stem: In which direction does the arrow point when representing a coordinate covalent bond?
rationales: Incorrect: the arrow points away from the donor and towards the acceptor.
Correct: the arrow head points towards the acceptor.
Incorrect: two parallel lines represent a double covalent bond.
Incorrect: a plus sign is not the section's symbol for a coordinate covalent bond.

rationales: Correct: sodium loses an electron to become Na⁺, and chlorine gains it to become Cl⁻.

explain.title: What is a chemical bond?
explain.body: A chemical bond is a force of attraction between atoms which holds them together in the form of a molecule or a compound.

explain.title: Ionic bonds form by electron transfer
explain.body: An ionic bond is formed when atoms lose or gain electron(s) to acquire the electronic configuration of the nearest noble gas. The resulting oppositely charged ions are held together by electrostatic attraction.

explain.title: Covalent bonds form by sharing
explain.body: A covalent bond is a bond formed by the mutual sharing of an electron pair provided by the bonded atoms. One shared pair makes a single bond; two and three shared pairs make double and triple bonds.

explain.title: Coordinate covalent bonds have one donor
explain.body: Coordinate covalent bond is a type of covalent bond in which the shared electron pair is donated by one atom only. The donating species is the donor and the accepting species is the acceptor. An arrow points towards the acceptor.

explain.title: Polar and non-polar covalent bonds
explain.body: When a covalent bond is formed between two identical atoms, the shared pair lies midway between them and the bond is non-polar. Between non-identical atoms, the shared pair bends towards the more electronegative atom, making the bond polar.

mistakes: Do not describe an ionic bond as sharing electrons; it forms by complete transfer of electron(s).
Do not say that the whole ionic compound is one positive or negative ion; it contains oppositely charged ions.
Do not reverse the direction of a coordinate-bond arrow; it points towards the acceptor.
Do not confuse a double bond (=) with a triple bond (≡).
Do not say the two electrons in a coordinate shared pair come from different atoms; both are donated by one atom.
When explaining a polar covalent bond, state that the shared pair bends towards the more electronegative atom.
